card.category: paid one-time media centre app for Apple platforms, Stremio addon API, debrid-aware
card.summary: No free tier: 'USD 4.99 · Designed for iPad'. One-time App Store purchase, no subscription line on the listing.

record.category: paid one-time media centre app for Apple platforms, Stremio addon API, debrid-aware

free_tier.stated: No free tier: 'USD 4.99 · Designed for iPad'. One-time App Store purchase, no subscription line on the listing.
free_tier.notes: A regional price was seen only through a search index (INR 499 on the Indian storefront); the USD 4.99 is from the US listing read directly.

retention.stated: not applicable: progress syncs through iCloud; media stays with the debrid provider

egress.terms: No allowance: playback goes to whatever URL the installed addon returns. The app itself carries no traffic.

record.interface_detail: 'Currently Vidi only supports addons using the Stremio addon API', with a subset documented on the vendor site. Native player with 'HDR10, HDR10+, and Dolby Vision'; progress syncs 'between your devices with iCloud'.
record.tooling: App Store install for iPhone, iPad, Mac (Apple silicon), Apple TV and Vision. No server, no web app.
record.chaining: The Apple-platform front end for the same addon URL a Stremio client would use: the debrid key lives inside the addon, so one key serves Vidi on an Apple TV and Stremio Web anywhere else.

limits.value: the App Store purchase is the gate; after it, the app imposes no published request or byte limit

record.limits_note: The addon-API subset is the functional limit: an addon that relies on parts of the Stremio API Vidi does not implement will install and then misbehave, which is a support burden rather than a measurable cap.
record.binding_note: Nothing here counts bytes or requests; any 1 TiB/month wall is met at the addon or the debrid provider, not at the player.

identity_cost.detail: Apple ID with a payment method for a USD 4.99 purchase. No account with the developer.

record.reliability_note: A single-developer App Store app: the risk is abandonment and iOS-version drift, not quota. It reached the App Store, which most addon front ends never do.
record.confidence_note: The US App Store listing and the vendor site were read. Not measured: installation and playback, and which addons pass the API subset.

evidence.proved: the price and platform list: '$4.99', 'Designed for iPad', iOS 17+/iPadOS 17+/macOS 14+ (M1)/tvOS 17+/visionOS 1.0+, 'Currently Vidi only supports addons using the Stremio addon API', iCloud progress sync, HDR10/HDR10+/Dolby Vision
'Purchase once and get it for all supported platforms', 'Family sharing enabled', 'No subscriptions', 'Supports Stremio Addons', 'Available on iOS, iPadOS and tvOS'
reported, not read: a search index shows the Indian storefront listing '₹ 499', which would make the price regional rather than a single global number

record.notes: The only debrid front end with a publishable per-month cost of essentially zero after the first year: USD 4.99 once, versus USD 9/month for a hosted addon or USD 24/month for a hosted stack. It is the cheapest way to get a TV-native player with no server to run, on a device in Apple's ecosystem.

extras.license_shape: one purchase, all platforms, family sharing, no subscription
extras.alternatives_seen: Streamyfin, Infuse, Swiftfin, Odin (Jellyfin clients, not debrid front ends)
